web_title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: Chapter 5: The Operator's Dashboard — KPIs, Management Quotes & Accountability
question: What do Mondelēz's operational KPIs and 2022–2026 management track record tell us about execution quality and structural runway?

epigraph.quote: Volume is the oxygen of a consumer franchise; pricing can mask a cold for a year, but only household penetration builds lasting wealth.
epigraph.author: Consumer Franchise Underwriting Maxim

web_blocks.html: Evaluating Mondelēz requires separating temporary commodity-cycle noise from underlying franchise health across six leading operational KPIs. Those six KPIs are Organic Net Revenue Growth, Volume/Mix vs. Pricing balance, Adjusted Gross Margin, Adjusted Operating Income Margin, Free Cash Flow Conversion, and Share-of-Revenue Gaining or Holding Share. In FY2025, +8.0 pp of cocoa-driven pricing pushed volume/mix down -3.7 pp [10]. By Q3 2026, Mondelēz inflected back to +1.8 pp positive volume/mix growth (+2.1% organic revenue) [12]. Adjusted Gross Margin expanded +380 bps YoY to 34.2%, while Adjusted OI Margin rose +190 bps to 13.9% [12]. Critically, the share of Mondelēz's snacking revenue gaining or holding market share rebounded from roughly 40% in FY2025 to ~65% YTD in 2026 [23].

web_blocks.caption: Leading Operational KPIs Trajectory (FY2023–Q3 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: Q3 2026 marks a clear operational inflection: volume/mix turned positive (+1.8 pp) and adjusted gross margin expanded +380 bps as cocoa relief began flowing through.

web_blocks.html: A granular look at the 2025–2026 quarterly cadence confirms that Q3 2026 was a progressive turn rather than a one-quarter anomaly [10, 12, 23, 33]. In Q4 2025, aggressive pricing (+9.9 pp) pushed volume/mix down -4.8 pp [10]. In Q1 2026, organic revenue grew +3.0% (+3.5 pp pricing, -0.5 pp vol/mix), with emerging markets up +6.3% [17, 33]. In Q2 2026, organic growth held at +2.2%, driven by Gum & Candy (+7.6%) and Biscuits (+2.5%) [23]. By Q3 2026, pricing moderated to +0.3 pp while volume/mix surged to +1.8 pp—the strongest volume-led quarter since the cocoa spike began [12]. That rebound proved that consumers returned to core brands once shelf prices stabilized [12].

Capital-allocation and innovation KPIs reinforce that operational picture. Management's bolt-on M&A filter targets acquisitions up to $0.5 billion–$1.0 billion in revenue in white-space segments rather than transformative mega-deals [12, 26]. The October 2026 agreement to acquire Undercover Snacks—a gluten-free, chocolate-covered crispy quinoa snack sold on United Airlines and at Whole Foods, Target, and Walmart—exemplifies that approach [12, 26]. Operated as a standalone unit within North American ventures alongside Tate's, Perfect Snacks, and Hu, Undercover Snacks shows how Mondelēz uses procurement and retail scale to compound emerging better-for-you brands without disrupting core operations [12, 26].

Regional execution KPIs in Q3 2026 underscore how broad-based the operational recovery has become [12]. In AMEA, organic net revenue rose +7.7% (+5.5 pp volume/mix), led by double-digit momentum in India and resilient emerging-market consumer confidence [12, 17]. In North America, organic revenue grew +1.6% even as low-income consumer traffic stayed soft [12]. Management tightened promotional depth and frequency—eliminating unprofitable trade-down between regular and promoted prices—while gaining share in Ritz, Ritz Minis, Sour Patch Kids, and Zbar [12].

web_blocks.title: Verbatim Management Commentary (Q3 2026 Earnings Call, Oct 29, 2026)
paragraphs: Dirk Van de Put (Chairman & CEO) on emerging markets & distribution: "Year-to-date, I think we've added about 130,000 outlets in India. Brazil, we're now over 1 million stores. And in China, we still have a very long runway. So we keep on doing that." [12]

Luca Zaramella (COO; CFO through June 2026) on emerging-market runway & Europe pricing: "The runway that we have in places like China, India, Brazil, it is most likely we still have 25% numeric distribution to go... What matters to us is to keep the penetration of our brand and the loyalty of our consumers into our brand. And as we look at penetration numbers, as we look at share results, clearly, for me, at least, that was the right decision to be made." [12]

Amit Banati (CFO, appointed July 2026) on cocoa supply & 2027 recovery: "If you look at the '25, '26 cycle, we expect to be ending this year with a surplus of almost 0.5 million tons, so 500,000 tons, which is a record level of surplus... We remain confident that we are going to drive strong EPS growth in '27. I think that's going to be on the back of volume-led growth into the year." [12]

web_blocks.takeaway: Management has a high-credibility track record on capital portfolio pruning, FCF delivery, and emerging-market execution; North American biscuit/bar volume velocity remains the primary execution watchpoint.

web_blocks.html: Executive Incentive Alignment & Insider Activity (2026 DEF 14A & Form 4s): Per the 2026 Proxy Statement (DEF 14A), Mondelēz ties 75% of Long-Term Incentives to 3-year Performance Share Units. Those PSUs split 50% Organic Net Revenue Growth and 50% Adjusted EPS Growth, with a 25-point relative TSR modifier [35]. The Annual Incentive Plan weights Adjusted Gross Profit (35%), Free Cash Flow (20%), Organic Volume (15%), Revenue (15%), and Adjusted OI (15%) [35]. Neither plan includes an explicit ROIC or net-leverage hurdle, creating a bias toward debt-funded buybacks [10, 35]. On insider activity, Form 4 filings show CEO Dirk Van de Put exercised options and sold 258,570 shares across November 2–5, 2026 [36, 37]. COO Luca Zaramella also exercised 22,410 options on November 2, 2026, with 18,110 shares withheld for taxes [36, 37].

book_paragraphs: When you and I evaluate a management team, we don't grade them on how smoothly they read a teleprompter during boom times. We grade them on how their operational dashboard holds up under stress—and whether their promises from three years ago match today's cash flow statement.

Look at Mondelēz's six core operational KPIs from 2023 through late 2026. During the 2025 cocoa storm, organic revenue still grew 4.3%, but it was entirely price-driven: pricing jumped 8.0 percentage points while volume and mix fell 3.7 points. Adjusted gross margin compressed 580 basis points to 32.0%, and the share of Mondelēz's revenue holding or gaining market share slipped to roughly 40%. Fast-forward to the third quarter of 2026, and the inflection is unmistakable. Volume and mix turned positive at +1.8 percentage points, adjusted gross margin expanded 380 basis points year-over-year to 34.2%, and the percentage of revenue holding or gaining market share climbed back to roughly 65%.

Listen to how leadership framed this pivot on the October 29, 2026 earnings call. CEO Dirk Van de Put highlighted the physical distribution grind: 'Year-to-date, I think we've added about 130,000 outlets in India. Brazil, we're now over 1 million stores. And in China, we still have a very long runway.' Meanwhile, Luca Zaramella—who served as CFO for eight years before stepping up to Chief Operating Officer in July 2026—explained why management accepted near-term price givebacks in Europe: 'What matters to us is to keep the penetration of our brand and the loyalty of our consumers into our brand.' And new CFO Amit Banati, formerly of Kenvue, confirmed that the 2025/2026 cocoa crop is ending with a record 500,000-ton surplus, setting up volume-led earnings growth in 2027.

Now let's run a cold-blooded Walk-the-Talk audit on Dirk Van de Put's team over the past four years. On portfolio pruning, they earned an A: they promised to exit low-growth developed-market gum and monetize their non-core JDE Peet's coffee stake, and they executed both cleanly in 2023 and 2024. On 2024 guidance, they hit every target: 4.3% organic growth, 13% constant-currency adjusted EPS growth, and $3.52 billion in free cash flow. In 2025, even as cocoa costs crushed GAAP earnings, they still delivered $3.24 billion in free cash flow.

Where is the blemish? North America. Despite paying $2.9 billion for Clif Bar in 2022, North American organic revenue slipped 1.9% in 2025, and the Clif Bar earn-out liability on the September 2026 balance sheet stood at just $111 million against a theoretical $2.4 billion ceiling—a clear signal that initial growth expectations were tempered by category softness. While Ritz, Sour Patch Kids, and Zbar gained share in Q3 2026, sustained North American volume growth remains the one operational box management still has to prove.

Tracing the quarter-by-quarter progression from late 2025 through Q3 2026 makes that operational turn even clearer. In the fourth quarter of 2025, Mondelēz pushed pricing up nearly 10% across the portfolio, and volumes fell 4.8% in response. By Q1 2026, pricing eased to +3.5% and volume contraction narrowed to -0.5%. By Q3 2026, pricing flattened to +0.3% and volume/mix swung all the way back to +1.8% growth. That is textbook elasticity recovery: when you protect brand equity with advertising during an inflationary spike, consumers come back as soon as price gaps normalize.

At the same time, management has been transparent about near-term headwinds heading into 2027. On the Q3 2026 call, Amit Banati noted that while cocoa is entering a 500,000-ton surplus, Mondelēz is still absorbing elevated Middle East-related energy and freight costs as well as inflation in dairy, oil, and packaging. Yet the combination of volume-led operating leverage, supply-chain productivity, and rolling off 2025 cocoa hedges gives management high confidence in strong EPS growth for 2027.

The October 2026 deal for Undercover Snacks is a great window into how Dirk Van de Put thinks about innovation and capital allocation. Undercover makes gluten-free, allergy-friendly crispy quinoa snacks coated in chocolate—the kind of better-for-you treat you might have eaten on a United Airlines flight or spotted at Whole Foods. It is small today, and management openly told analysts it will not move the financial needle in 2027.

So why buy it? Because Mondelēz runs a dedicated North American ventures incubator—housing Tate's Bake Shop, Perfect Snacks, and Hu—where founders stay in charge while Mondelēz plugs them into lower-cost chocolate procurement and national supermarket distribution. Instead of trying to invent trendy better-for-you brands inside a $38 billion bureaucracy, Mondelēz buys proven product-market fit early and scales it.

Let's zoom in on North America's promotional turnaround in Q3 2026, because it is a textbook example of operational discipline. Throughout 2025, several packaged-food peers tried to buy back lost U.S. volumes by slashing list prices or running deep buy-one-get-one promotions. Mondelēz refused to cut list prices. Instead, as COO Luca Zaramella explained on the Q3 2026 call, the team overhauled the depth and frequency of its promotions to eliminate wasteful cannibalization where regular buyers simply waited for discounts.

The result? North America posted +1.6% organic growth with flat volume/mix and rising gross profit dollars—even while the broader U.S. consumer environment remained soft and K-shaped. Combine that with +7.7% organic growth in AMEA (driven by +5.5 percentage points of pure volume and mix), and you can see why management's operational credibility has strengthened heading into 2027.

A forensic look at the 2026 Proxy Statement also reveals an important governance nuance in how executives are paid. Seventy-five percent of long-term equity awards sit in three-year Performance Share Units split equally between Organic Net Revenue Growth and Adjusted EPS Growth, while the annual bonus weights Adjusted Gross Profit, Free Cash Flow, Organic Volume, Revenue, and Operating Income. What is missing from both scorecards is an explicit Return on Invested Capital or net-leverage target—which helps explain why management has willingly used incremental borrowing to fund share repurchases that lift Adjusted EPS even when payouts exceed organic Free Cash Flow. Meanwhile, November 2026 Form 4 filings show CEO Dirk Van de Put exercising options and selling 258,570 shares between November 2 and November 5, 2026, alongside routine option exercises by COO Luca Zaramella.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why the CFO-to-COO Promotion Matters
book_callouts.text: When a consumer-goods company promotes its long-tenured CFO (Luca Zaramella) to Chief Operating Officer and brings in an external veteran CFO (Amit Banati), it usually signals a shift from financial defense to operational execution—tightening supply-chain productivity, ERP rollout, and Revenue Growth Management across regions.
